proposals: The Department of Commerce should publish the targets its NIRYAT portal scores each country and commodity against, as a downloadable table, so that whether a bilateral relationship such as China’s −$112.2 billion deficit is “on track” can be checked against a stated goal.

MeitY should publish, each year, China’s share of India’s electronic-component imports alongside PLI electronics outcomes, so that the estimated 62% dependence, now known only from industry reporting, is tracked as an official outcome measure of the scheme.

The Department of Commerce should offer TRADESTAT and Trade Intelligence & Analytics country-by-commodity data as bulk downloads for all trading partners, so that analyses like this one need not be limited to 38 of about 217 partners or rely on session workarounds to extract tables.

The RBI should publish an annual breakdown of merchandise import payments by settlement currency for major partner countries, so that arrangements such as paying for Russian crude in UAE dirhams are measured in official data rather than described only in press reporting.
